rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge extends into the future: they will never produce what is demanded, so they must beware the Fire.
rows.anchor: ه أيضا فيما يستقبل أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To fear the Fire is to guard against reaching it.
rows.anchor: فاحذروا أن تصلوا { النار التي وقودها } ما يوقد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones serving as fuel are sulfur stones, which catch fire especially intensely.
rows.anchor: يعني حجارة الكبريت، وهي أشد لاتقادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire was created and prepared as recompense for those who disbelieve by denial.
rows.anchor: [خلقت وهيئت] جزاء { للكافرين } بتكذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving glad tidings means announcing news whose joyful effect appears on the recipients’ faces.
rows.anchor: أخبرهم خبرا يظهر به أثر السرور على بشرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous deeds are acts of obedience performed between people and their Lord.
rows.anchor: يعني الطاعات فيما بينهم وبين ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens are orchards with trees.
rows.anchor: حدائق ذات الشجر { تجري من تحتها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers flow beneath the gardens’ trees and dwellings.
rows.anchor: من تحت أشجارها ومساكنها { الأنهار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being provided with fruit means being fed fruit from those gardens.
rows.anchor: أطعموا من تلك الجنات ثمرة

words: قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى رُزِقْنَا مِن قَبْلُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They recognize the fruit as like what they received before because it resembles that earlier provision in kind.
rows.anchor: وأرادوا: هذا من نوع ما رزقنا من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruits resemble one another in color and form but differ in taste, increasing their wonder.
rows.anchor: وذلك أبلغ في باب الإعجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their spouses include both houris and human women.
rows.anchor: من الحور العين والآدميات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are free of worldly women’s harm and filth, bad character, and the afflictions of greying and old age.
rows.anchor: ومن مساوىء الأخلاق، وآفات الشيب والهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remain forever because the perfection of a blessing depends on its permanence.
rows.anchor: وهم فيها خالدون } لأن تمام النعمة بالخلود

words: خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created everything on earth for people: some things are for use and others for reflection.
rows.anchor: ما في الأرض جميعا } بعضها للانتفاع، وبعضها للاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here istawā ilā means that God turned toward creating heaven and directed Himself to it.
rows.anchor: أقبل على خلقها، وقصد إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He made the seven heavens even and well-proportioned, without fissures, cracks, or disparity.
rows.anchor: فجعلهن سبع سموات مستويات لا شقوق فيها ولا فطور ولا تفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge makes the perfectly ordered act possible.
rows.anchor: إذ بالعلم يصح الفعل المحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad to recall and tell them when his Lord spoke to the angels.
rows.anchor: واذكر لهم يا محمد إذ قال ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The khalīfa is Adam, successor to the angels who had inhabited the earth after the jinn; the story recalls the beginning of human creation.
rows.anchor: جعله خليفة عن الملائكة الذين كانوا سكان الأرض بعد الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels anticipated human corruption by analogy with the jinn, reasoning from the known to the unseen.
rows.anchor: كما فعل بنو الجان، قاسوا [الشاهد] على الغائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels declare God free of every evil and say, Glory and praise belong to God.
rows.anchor: نبرئك من كل سوء، ونقول: سبحان الله وبحمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They declare God transcendent above whatever is unbefitting Him.
rows.anchor: وننزهك عما لا يليق بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God knew and the angels did not was Iblis’s concealed resolve to disobey.
rows.anchor: من إضمار إبليس العزم على المعصية

words: قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels privately concluded that their Lord would create no creature more knowledgeable than they were.
rows.anchor: لن يخلق ربنا خلقا هو أعلم منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God favored Adam over the angels through knowledge and taught him the names of every thing, down to ordinary utensils.
rows.anchor: وعلمه اسم كل شيء حتى القصعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forty nights refer to the completion of the appointed period for God to speak with Moses.
rows.anchor: أي: انقضاءها وتمامها للتكلم معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people made the calf their object of worship after Moses left them for the appointed meeting.
rows.anchor: من بعد خروجه عنكم للميقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their injustice was putting worship in the wrong place.
rows.anchor: واضعون العبادة في غير موضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disbelief in Muhammad is no more astonishing than their calf worship during Moses’s lifetime.
rows.anchor: وهذا تنبيه على أن كفرهم بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ليس بأعجب من كفرهم وعبادتهم العجل في زمن موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God erased their sins after they worshipped the calf so that they might be grateful for His favor of pardon.
rows.anchor: لكي تشكروا نعمتي بالعفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the Furqan is an explanatory apposition: it means the Torah.
rows.anchor: يعني: التوراة الفارق بين [الحق والباطل]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah distinguishes truth from falsehood and the lawful from the unlawful, guiding them away from error.
rows.anchor: والحلال والحرام { لعلكم تهتدون } لكي تهتدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses addressed the people who had worshipped the calf and said that taking it as a deity was self-wronging.
rows.anchor: الذين عبدوا العجل { يا قوم إنكم ظلمتم أنفسكم باتخاذكم العجل } إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their bāriʾ is their Creator.
rows.anchor: يعني: خالقكم. قالوا: كيف نتوب؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The innocent among them were to kill those who had committed the calf worship.
rows.anchor: أي: ليقتل البريء منكم المجرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Carrying out this repentance was better for them than remaining in calf worship; they did what they were ordered.
rows.anchor: من إقامتكم على عبادة العجل، ثم فعلتم ما أمرتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted their repentance; He is the One who accepts repentance and is merciful.
rows.anchor: قبل توبتكم. { إنه هو التواب الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers were the men Moses selected to apologize to God for the calf worship; they spoke after hearing God and after Moses finished his communion.
rows.anchor: الذين اختارهم موسى عليه السلام ليعتذروا إلى الله سبحانه من عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They told Moses they would not believe or affirm what he said.
rows.anchor: لن نصدقك { حتى نرى الله جهرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demanded to see God visibly, with nothing veiling Him from them.
rows.anchor: أي: عيانا لا يستره عنا شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣāʿiqa was a fire sent down from heaven that burned them all.
rows.anchor: وهي نار جاءت من السماء فأحرقتهم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were looking at the ṣāʿiqa as it descended.
rows.anchor: إليها حين نزلت، وإنما أخذتهم الصاعقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were punished for refusing faith in Moses after his miracle appeared and demanding that God be shown openly; faith in prophets is obligatory after a miracle, and demanding further miracles is impermissible.
rows.anchor: والإيمان بالأنبياء واجب بعد ظهور معجزتهم، ولا يجوز اقتراح المعجزات عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes their disobedience to the Messenger despite his established miracle, as their ancestors disobeyed Moses despite manifest signs.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية توبيخ لهم على مخالفة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is not lightened either in this world or in the next.
rows.anchor: معناه: في الدنيا والآخرة، وقيل: هذه الحالة مختصة بالآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reported view restricts the unlightened punishment to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذه الحالة مختصة بالآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogating a verse means removing it by invalidating its ruling.
rows.anchor: ما نرفع آية من جهة النسخ بأن نبطل حكمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causing a verse to be forgotten means erasing it from people’s hearts.
rows.anchor: أو بالإنساء لها بأن نمحوها عن القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A better replacement is more suitable and useful for those charged with it, easier for them, and greater in reward.
rows.anchor: أصلح لمن تعبد بها، وأنفع لهم وأسهل عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An equivalent replacement matches it in benefit and reward.
rows.anchor: أو مثلها } في المنفعة والمثوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed after polytheists alleged that Muhammad gave his Companions a command and then reversed it, proving the Quran was his own speech.
rows.anchor: حين قال المشركون: إن محمدا يأمر أصحابه بأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary links the abrogation discussion to the statement about replacing one verse with another.
rows.anchor: وقوله: وإذا بدلنا آية مكان آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership of the heavens and earth means He acts as He wills and knows what is beneficial in the obligations He gives through abrogation and replacement.
rows.anchor: وهو أعلم بوجه الصلاح فيما يتعبدهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apart from God, no guardian manages your affairs and no helper can aid you; this warns that none can block His punishment.
rows.anchor: ينصركم، وفي هذا تحذير من عذابه إذ لا مانع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to be Muslims in the sense of obedient and submissive to God’s command.
rows.anchor: مسلمين لك } مطيعين منقادين لحكمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslim community from their descendants is identified as the emigrants, the Helpers, and those who follow them in goodness.
rows.anchor: وهم المهاجرون والأنصار والتابعون بإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask God to teach them their acts of worship.
rows.anchor: عرفنا متعبداتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people among whom the messenger is sent are the Muslim community, and the messenger is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يريد: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book and wisdom here mean the Quran, which the messenger recites and teaches.
rows.anchor: ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة } أي: القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purifying them means cleansing them of associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: ويزكيهم } ويطهرهم من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means the prevailing, powerful one whom nothing can defeat; the meaning of al-Ḥakīm was explained earlier.
rows.anchor: الغالب القوي الذي لا يعجزه شيء، ومضى تفسير الحكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means that none turns away from Abraham’s religion and abandons it except one who makes himself foolish.
rows.anchor: أي: وما يرغب عنها ولا يتركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a person is ignorant of himself, failing to know that God created him and that he must worship his Creator.
rows.anchor: جهلها بأن لم يعلم أنها مخلوقة لله تعالى يجب عليها عبادة خالقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God selected Abraham for prophethood in this world.
rows.anchor: اخترناه للرسالة { وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous people in the afterlife are the prophets.
rows.anchor: وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين } أي: من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation preserves life: a would-be killer is deterred, saving the intended victim and the killer from execution.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن القاتل إذا قتل ارتدع عن القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulū al-albāb means people endowed with reason.
rows.anchor: يا ذوي العقول { لعلكم تتقون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may avoid shedding blood out of fear of retaliation.
rows.anchor: لعلكم تتقون } [إراقة] الدماء مخافة القصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse responded to pre-Islamic Arabs who left their relatives poor while bequeathing wealth to distant people for show and reputation.
rows.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يوصون بمالهم للبعداء رياء وسمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bequest was initially prescribed and made obligatory.
rows.anchor: فرض عليكم وأوجب { إذا حضر أحدكم الموت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death arriving means its causes and preliminaries have appeared.
rows.anchor: إذا حضر أحدكم الموت } أي: أسبابه ومقدماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here khayr means wealth.
rows.anchor: مالا { الوصية للوالدين والأقربين بالمعروف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bequest to parents and relatives should be reasonable and must not exceed one third of the estate.
rows.anchor: يعني: لا يزيد على الثلث { حقا } أي: حق ذلك حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty is placed on the God-fearing, whom the author characterizes here as those who avoid associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: على المتقين } الذين يتقون الشرك، وهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance verse abrogated this rule; a bequest is not obligatory and may not be made for an heir.
rows.anchor: ولا تجب الوصية على أحد، [ولا تجوز الوصية للوارث]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fasting prescribed is the fast of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: يعني صيام شهر رمضان { كما كتب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community is charged with fasting just as earlier peoples were charged with it.
rows.anchor: أي: أنتم متعبدون بالصيام كما تعبد من قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting is so they will avoid eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse during the period when fasting is obligatory.
rows.anchor: لكي تتقوا الأكل والشرب والجماع في وقت وجوب الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The numbered days are the month of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: أياما معدودات } يعني: شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sick person or traveler who breaks the fast must make up the corresponding number of days later.
rows.anchor: فعليه عدة، أي: صوم عدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the beginning of Islam, anyone able to fast could instead break the fast and feed one poor person a mudd of food for each day.
rows.anchor: هذا كان في ابتداء الإسلام؛ من أطاق الصوم جاز له أن يفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the ruling was abrogated, giving more than one mudd as the expiation was an added good.
rows.anchor: زاد في الفدية على مد واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before abrogation, fasting was better than breaking the fast and paying the food expiation.
rows.anchor: والصوم خير لكم من الإفطار والفدية، وهذا [إنما] كان قبل النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier choice to pay a food expiation instead of fasting was abrogated by the command to fast when one witnesses Ramadan.
rows.anchor: فنسخ بقوله: { فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan is the numbered-days period mentioned in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: هي شهر رمضان. يعني: تلك الأيام المعدودات شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran descended as a whole from the Preserved Tablet on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan, was placed in the lower heaven’s Bayt al-ʿIzza, then Gabriel brought it to Muhammad in installments over twenty years.
rows.anchor: أنزل جملة واحد من اللوح المحفوظ في ليلة القدر من شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is guidance in the sense that it guides people.
rows.anchor: هدى للناس } هاديا للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its clear signs explain the lawful and unlawful, prescribed limits, and rulings.
rows.anchor: وآيات واضحات من الحلال والحرام، والحدود والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Furqān is the distinction between truth and falsehood.
rows.anchor: والفرقان } الفرق بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing the month means being present in one’s own town during it; such a person must fast.
rows.anchor: فمن حضر منكم بلده في الشهر

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sick and travelers retain the earlier dispensation because the earlier verse gave them and residents a choice, while this verse abrogated the resident’s choice.
rows.anchor: لأن الآية الأولى وردت في التخيير للمريض والمسافر والمقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills ease through the concession for a sick person or traveler.
rows.anchor: بالرخصة للمسافر والمريض { ولا يريد بكم العسر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not intend hardship because He has neither imposed strictness nor narrowed matters for them.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يشدد ولم يضيق عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is joined to an omitted clause; the sense is that God wills ease rather than hardship so that people can complete the count.
rows.anchor: [عطف على محذوف] والمعنى: يريد الله بكم اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They complete the count of missed fasts through make-up days after settling from travel or recovering.
rows.anchor: أي: ولتكملوا عدة ما أفطرتم بالقضاء إذا أقمتم وبرأتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded magnification is the takbīr on the night of Eid al-Fitr when the crescent of Shawwal is sighted.
rows.anchor: يعني التكبير ليلة الفطر إذا رئي هلال شوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided them to the religious laws.
rows.anchor: على ما هداكم } أرشدكم من شرائع الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs generally departed from Arafat, but Quraysh stayed at Muzdalifah, claiming that the people of the sanctuary should not leave it; God ordered Quraysh to stand at Arafat and depart with everyone else.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا لا يقفون بعرفات وإنما يقفون بالمزدلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means finishing the acts of worship commanded in the pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: أي: فرغتم من عباداتكم التي أمرتم بها في الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After pilgrimage, Arabs used to recount their fathers’ boasts, so God commanded them instead to remember Him.
rows.anchor: كانت العرب إذا فرغوا من حجهم ذكروا مفاخر آبائهم، فأمرهم الله عز وجل بذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means to remember God even more intensely.
rows.anchor: أو أشد ذكرا } يعني: وأشد ذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These people are polytheists who ask for wealth, camels, and sheep but no share in the afterlife, since they do not believe in it; Muslims ask for good in both worlds.
rows.anchor: وهم المشركون كانوا يسألون المال والإبل والغنم، ولا يسألون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fighting, meaning jihad, is imposed as an obligation.
rows.anchor: كتب عليكم القتال } فرض وأوجب عليكم الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fighting is difficult because it burdens one’s person and property.
rows.anchor: أي: مشقة عليكم لما يدخل منه على النفس والمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A disliked campaign can bring one of two good outcomes: victory and spoils, or martyrdom and Paradise.
rows.anchor: لأن في الغزو إحدى الحسنيين؛ إما الظفر والغنيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they might prefer is staying home from battle, which brings humiliation, poverty, and loss of spoils and reward.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من الذل والفقر، وحرمان الغنيمة والأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows where their interests lie, so they should promptly obey His commands even when difficult.
rows.anchor: ما فيه مصالحكم، فبادروا إلى ما يأمركم به وإن شق عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse followed an expedition sent by the Messenger that fought polytheists after the Rajab crescent appeared, without realizing the month had begun; the polytheists made an issue of bloodshed in Rajab.
rows.anchor: نزلت في سرية بعثها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقاتلوا المشركين وقد أهل هلال رجب وهم لا يعلمون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people asking about the sacred month are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: يعني: المشركين. وقيل: هم المسلمون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative view identifies the questioners as Muslims.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم المسلمون { عن الشهر الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question concerns fighting during the sacred month, which is a grave matter.
rows.anchor: أي: وعن قتال فيه { قل قتال فيه كبير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here turning people from God’s way means preventing them from obeying Him; the polytheists blocked the Messenger and Companions from the Sacred House at al-Hudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: يعني: صد المشركين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists disbelieved in God and obstructed access to the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: بالله { والمسجد الحرام } أي: وصد عن المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people driven out of the mosque’s precincts were the Messenger and his Companions, expelled from Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعني: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه حين أخرجوا من مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obstructing the way of God, disbelief, blocking the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people are greater sins before God than the expedition’s killing in Rajab.
rows.anchor: أكبر من القتل } يعني: قتل السرية المشركين في رجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna here means associating partners with God, and it is worse than killing.
rows.anchor: الفتنة } أي: والشرك { أكبر من القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists keep fighting the believers in order to turn them back to disbelief if they can.
rows.anchor: يعني: المشركين { يقاتلونكم حتى يردوكم عن دينكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns one who leaves Islam and dies in disbelief, whose deeds are nullified.
rows.anchor: أي: يرجع فيموت على الكفر { فأولئك حبطت أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The members of the expedition asked the Messenger whether, after striking the polytheists in Rajab, they could hope for the reward of those who strive in God’s way.
rows.anchor: فقال هؤلاء السرية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe are the ones who accept faith in God.
rows.anchor: فارقوا عشائرهم وأوطانهم { وجاهدوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Migration means leaving one’s clan and homeland.
rows.anchor: فارقوا عشائرهم وأوطانهم { وجاهدوا } المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Striving in God’s way means fighting the polytheists to support God’s religion.
rows.anchor: في نصرة دين الله { أولئك يرجون رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expedition members hope for God’s mercy, and God forgave them for what they had done unknowingly and showed them mercy.
rows.anchor: غفر لهؤلاء السرية ما لم يعلموا ورحمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consensus is now that fighting polytheists is permitted in all months, whether sacred or not.
rows.anchor: والإجماع اليوم منعقد على أن قتال المشركين يجوز في جميع الأشهر حلالها وحرامها

rows.speaker: عمر، ومعاذ، وسعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: ʿUmar, Muʿādh, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ asked the Messenger for a ruling because wine and gambling destroy reason and strip away wealth.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عمر، ومعاذ، وسعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine is any intoxicant that mixes with and overcomes the intellect.
rows.anchor: وهو كل مسكر مخالط للعقل مغط عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir means gambling.
rows.anchor: الميسر }: القمار { قل فيهما إثم كبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sin includes the quarrels, insults, obscene speech, falsehood, and other evils they cause.
rows.anchor: الإثم بسببهما لما فيهما من المخاصمة والمشاتمة وقول الفحش والزور وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine benefits sellers through money from trade and drinkers through pleasure; gambling yields winnings and can support poor people.
rows.anchor: ما كانوا يصيبونه من المال في بيع الخمر والتجارة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harms and sins caused by wine and gambling outweigh their benefits.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أن ما يحصل بسببهما من الإثم أكبر من نفعهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse did not itself prohibit wine and gambling; it preceded their prohibition in Sūrat al-Māʾida.
rows.anchor: وليست هذه الآية المحرمة للخمر والميسر، إنما المحرمة التي في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن الجموح
rows.claim: After the verse about spending for parents and relatives, ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ asked again how much should be spent.
rows.anchor: نزلت في سؤال عمرو بن الجموح لما نزل قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿafw is the money left over after providing for one’s dependents.
rows.anchor: أي: ما فضل من المال عن العيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this verse, a person kept enough from his earnings for his needs and gave away the remainder until zakat was prescribed.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل بعد نزول هذه الآية يأخذ من كسبه ما يكفيه، وينفق باقيه إلى أن فرضت الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zakat verse in Sūrat Barāʾa abrogated this instruction and the earlier commands to give charity before zakat.
rows.anchor: فنسخت آية الزكاة التي في براءة هذه الآية وكل صدقة أمروا بها قبل الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise may refer either to God’s explanation concerning wine and gambling or to His explanation about spending.
rows.anchor: أي: كبيانه في الخمر والميسر، أو في الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains the signs so people reflect on this world and the next and recognize the superiority of the afterlife over worldly life.
rows.anchor: لتتفكروا في أمر الدنيا والآخرة، فتعرفوا فضل الآخرة على الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening asks whether one has seen the dispute and its proof.
rows.anchor: جادل وخاصم { إبراهيم في ربه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To dispute means to argue and quarrel; the king asked Abraham who his Lord was.
rows.anchor: حين قال له: من ربك؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kingdom God gave him made him arrogant and provoked the dispute; the king was Nimrod son of Canaan.
rows.anchor: يريد: بطر الملك حمله على ذلك، وهو نمروذ بن كنعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham identified his Lord as the one who gives life and death; the enemy merely echoed the wording without actually causing life or death.
rows.anchor: فقال عدو الله: { أنا أحيي وأميت } فعارضه بالاشتراك

words: قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Nimrod blurred the argument by claiming the same power, Abraham gave an argument Nimrod could not imitate: command the sun to rise from the west.
rows.anchor: فلما لبس في الحجة بأن قال: أنا أفعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod was confounded and fell silent before Abraham’s challenge.
rows.anchor: فبهت الذي كفر } أي: انقطع وسكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that Jesus is also made a messenger to the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: أي: ويجعله رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word annī here means that he came to them with a sign from his Lord.
rows.anchor: أني } أي: بأني { قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating the bird-like form means measuring and shaping it into the bird’s likeness.
rows.anchor: أني أخلق } أي: أقدر وأصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-akmah is someone born blind.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي ولد أعمى { والأبرص }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-abraṣ is someone with al-ḍaḥ, a white skin patch.
rows.anchor: والأبرص } أي: الذي به وضح [أي: بياض]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them what they eat in the morning.
rows.anchor: في غدوكم { وما } كم { تدخرون } لباقي يومكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them what they store for the remainder of the day.
rows.anchor: كم { تدخرون } لباقي يومكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus came confirming the earlier scripture, the book revealed before him.
rows.anchor: وجئتكم مصدقا { لما بين يدي } أي: الكتاب الذي أنزل من قبلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through Jesus, camel meat, tripe, and some birds and fish were made lawful after being forbidden under Moses’s law.
rows.anchor: أحل لهم على لسان المسيح لحوم الإبل، والثروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’s signs were miracles proving his messengership; the verse uses a singular sign because all the miracles form one kind in their evidentiary force.
rows.anchor: أي: ما كان معه من المعجزات الدالة على رسالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness to parents means treating them well with gentleness.
rows.anchor: أحسنوا بهما إحسانا، وهو البر مع لين الجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A relative is to be visited and treated with affection.
rows.anchor: وهو ذو القرابة يصله ويتعطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphans should be treated gently and brought near.
rows.anchor: يرفق بهم ويدنيهم { والمساكين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor should receive a modest gift or a kind response.
rows.anchor: ببذل يسير، أو رد جميل { والجار ذي القربى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near relative neighbor has both the right of kinship and the right of neighborhood.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي له مع حق الجوار حق القرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distant neighbor is unrelated to one in lineage.
rows.anchor: البعيد عنك في النسب { والصاحب بالجنب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion by one’s side is a traveling companion.
rows.anchor: هو الرفيق في السفر { وابن السبيل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wayfarer is a traveler passing along the road.
rows.anchor: عابر الطريق. [وقيل: الضيف] يؤويه ويطعمه حتى يرحل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the wayfarer to mean a guest, whom one shelters and feeds until departure.
rows.anchor: [وقيل: الضيف] يؤويه ويطعمه حتى يرحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those possessed by the right hand are enslaved people.
rows.anchor: وما ملكت أيمانهم } أي: المماليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mukhtāl is self-important and neglects duties owed to God.
rows.anchor: عظيما في نفسه لا يقوم بحقوق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fakhūr boasts over God’s servants about the blessings God has bestowed on him.
rows.anchor: على عباده بما خوله الله من نعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who are miserly are the Jews, who withheld their wealth from spending in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: أي: اليهود. بخلوا بأموالهم أن ينفقوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They told the Helpers not to spend on the Messenger, warning that they feared the Helpers would become poor.
rows.anchor: أمروا الأنصار ألا ينفقوا أموالهم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they conceal is the Torah’s information about Muhammad and his description.
rows.anchor: أي: ما في التوراة من أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ونعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that time means on that Day; the people wished this after disobeying the Messenger in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي: في ذلك اليوم { يود الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wish they could become dust and merge with the earth as one substance.
rows.anchor: أي: يكونون ترابا، فيستوون مع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot conceal anything from God because their deeds are visible to Him.
rows.anchor: لأن ما عملوه ظاهر عند الله لا يقدرون على كتمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer here means the places of prayer, namely mosques.
rows.anchor: أي مواضع الصلاة، أي: المساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before wine was finally prohibited, Muslims were forbidden to pray or enter a mosque while drunk and avoided intoxication at prayer times.
rows.anchor: نهوا عن الصلاة وعن دخول المسجد في حال السكر، وكان هذا قبل نزول تحريم الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A drunk person has a confused mind, babbles, and cannot sustain speech; if one knows what one says, one is not drunk and may pray and enter the mosque.
rows.anchor: والسكران: المختلط العقل الذي يهذي، ولا يستمر كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person in major ritual impurity must not approach the mosque except to pass through without staying.
rows.anchor: إلا إذا عبرتم المسجد فدخلتموه من غير إقامة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction lasts until one performs the full ritual bath after major impurity.
rows.anchor: من الجنابة { وإن كنتم مرضى } أي: مرضا يضره الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relevant illness is one harmed by water, such as sores, smallpox, or wounds.
rows.anchor: أي: مرضا يضره الماء كالقروح، والجدري، والجراحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means being on a journey.
rows.anchor: أي: مسافرين { أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط }

words: أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌۭ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلْغَآئِطِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming from al-ghāʾiṭ means having a bodily event.
rows.anchor: أو الحدث { أو لامستم النساء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Touching women means touching them with one’s hands.
rows.anchor: { أو لامستم النساء } أي: لمستموهن بأيديكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When water is unavailable, perform dry ablution using clean earth that produces vegetation.
rows.anchor: تمسحوا بتراب طيب منبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given a portion of the Book are the Jews.
rows.anchor: وهم اليهود { يشترون الضلالة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They choose misguidance over guidance by denying Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أي: يختارونها على الهدى بتكذيب محمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They want the believers to stray from the path of guidance.
rows.anchor: أن تضلوا أيها المؤمنون طريق الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness for sins short of associating partners, forgiving whomever He wills; the author presents this against the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: وعد الله تعالى في هذه الآية مغفرة ما دون الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever associates partners with God has fabricated a grave sin that is not forgiven.
rows.anchor: أي: اختلق ذنبا غير مغفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those praising their own purity are Jews who claimed to be God’s children and beloved, and that their sins were erased by the opposite part of each day.
rows.anchor: أي: اليهود قالوا: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes whomever He wills pure and increases that person in righteousness; here this refers to monotheists.
rows.anchor: أي: يجعل من يشاء زاكيا طاهرا ناميا في الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not deprived of even a thread-thin amount of reward; fatīl is the thin membrane around a date pit.
rows.anchor: لا ينقصون من الثواب قدر الفتيل، وهو القشرة الرقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author transitions to the following verse by saying that the Prophet is made to marvel at their lies.
rows.anchor: ثم عجب نبيه عليه السلام من كذبهم، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When their skins are burned through, they are renewed to their former unburned condition.
rows.anchor: يعني: أن جلودهم إذا نضجت واحترقت جددت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To taste the punishment means to undergo and experience it.
rows.anchor: ليذوقوا العذاب } ليقاسوه وينالوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is powerful and none can overcome Him; He is wise in what He ordains.
rows.anchor: قويا لا يغلبه شيء { حكيما } فيما دبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deep shade is the air of Paradise, lasting because the sun never removes it.
rows.anchor: يعني: ظل هواء الجنة، وهو ظليل، أي: دائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed when the Kaaba key, forcibly taken from ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa al-Ḥajabī at the conquest of Mecca, was to be returned to him.
rows.anchor: نزلت في رد مفتاح الكعبة على عثمان بن طلحة الحجبي حين أخذ منه قسرا يوم فتح مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command applies generally: return trusts to their owners, whoever they may be.
rows.anchor: ثم هذه الآية عامة في رد الأمانات إلى أصحابها كيف ما كانوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording means what a good thing God admonishes you with, namely the Quran.
rows.anchor: أي: نعم شيئا يعظكم به، وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what people say about trusts and judgment and sees how they act regarding them.
rows.anchor: لمقالتكم في الأمانة والحكم { بصيرا } بما تعملون فيها

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abū Rawq reports that the Prophet asked ʿUthmān for the key, received it in trust, then intended to give it to al-ʿAbbās; after the verse descended, he returned it to ʿUthmān with the pledge that it would remain in his family until removed by an oppressor.
rows.anchor: قال أبو روق: " قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine here means drinks fermented until they become strong and intoxicating.
rows.anchor: يعني: الأشربة التي تخمر حتى تشتد وتسكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir means every kind of gambling.
rows.anchor: القمار بجميع أنواعه { والأنصاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anṣāb are idols.
rows.anchor: الأنصاب } الأوثان { والأزلام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The azlām are lots or arrows used for divination, mentioned at the beginning of this sūra.
rows.anchor: والأزلام } قداح الاستقسام التي ذكرت في أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs means something filthy and repugnant.
rows.anchor: رجس } قذر قبيح { من عمل الشيطان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These things belong to Satan’s work, which he tempts human beings to do.
rows.anchor: من عمل الشيطان } مما يسوله الشيطان لبني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoid it by keeping away from it altogether.
rows.anchor: فاجتنبوه } كونوا جانبا منه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine and gambling create enmity, hatred, quarrels, and other ugly conduct, including actions reason would forbid.
rows.anchor: وذلك لما يحصل بين أهلها من العداوة والمقابح، والإقدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They distract people from remembrance and prayer because involvement in them keeps people from both.
rows.anchor: لأن من اشتغل بهما منعاه عن ذكر الله والصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is phrased as an imperative; the people answered that they had stopped, after which obedience was commanded.
rows.anchor: [استفهام بمعنى الأمر] قالوا: انتهينا، ثم أمر بالطاعة

words: وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخُوضُونَ فِىٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disputatious talk means denying and mocking God’s signs.
rows.anchor: بالتكذيب والاستهزاء { فأعرض عنهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When polytheists deny the Quran and the Prophet and mock them, the Messenger must leave their company.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى رسوله عليه السلام فقال: إذا رأيت المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may be joined again when their discussion turns to something other than the Quran.
rows.anchor: حتى يكون خوضهم في غير القرآن { وإما ينسينك الشيطان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one forgets and stays seated, one should leave as soon as one remembers.
rows.anchor: إن نسيت فقعدت { فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى } فقم إذا ذكرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims said that withdrawing whenever the polytheists mocked the Quran would prevent them from sitting in the Sacred Mosque or circumambulating the House, so permission was given to remain if they admonished them.
rows.anchor: فقال المسلمون: لئن كنا كلما استهزأ المشركون بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers may sit with them on condition that they remind and admonish them with the Quran and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فرخص للمؤمنين في القعود معهم يذكرونهم فقال: { وما على الذين يتقون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear God are those who avoid associating partners with Him and major sins.
rows.anchor: الشرك والكبائر { من حسابهم } آثامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are only responsible for reminding the mockers through the Quran and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يقول: ذكروهم بالقرآن وبمحمد، فرخص لهم بالقعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase expresses hope that the mockers may become God-fearing.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يتقون } ليرجى منهم التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God splits the column of dawn from the darkness of night, meaning that He creates and brings dawn into being.
rows.anchor: شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل وسواده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made night a resting place where creatures sleep in repose.
rows.anchor: للخلق يسكنون فيه سكون الراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon move according to a reckoning and do not exceed the limits of their calculated courses.
rows.anchor: وجعل الشمس والقمر بحسبان لا يجاوزانه فيما يدوران في حساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the measure of the Mighty, who acts as He wills in His dominion, and the All-Knowing of what He has measured in creating them.
rows.anchor: في ملكه يصنع ما أراد { العليم } بما قدر من خلقهما
